thread:
sara: Heads-up — we saw a sharp p99 latency spike between GPU nodes during the 09:10-09:25 peak batching window in us-west2. Traces show grpc handshakes stalling for 200-400ms, then recover. Not full packet loss, more like tail spikes.

mike: Can you paste the node IDs? Any pattern by AZ or instance type?

sara: Node IDs: gpu-uw2a-12, gpu-uw2a-18, gpu-uw2b-03. All T4-like boxes (NVIDIA A10 equivalent), same kernel. Happens on cross-AZ east-west traffic and also within the same AZ but only when batching throughput > ~1.2k reqs/s.

kai: Seeing similar on canary this morning. ethtool -S showed tx_errors rising on the bursting node around the window. Not full drops, but tx_dropped and tx_queue_1 increases.

alex: Logs I grabbed: ```[ 12345.678901] igb 0000:03:00.0 eth0: Tx queue 0 is busy, disabling NAPI polls``` and ```netdev: peer 10.0.4.7 tx_queue stopped```. Also kernel netstat shows RPS offloading not applied on some cores.

mike: That looks like NIC transmit queue saturation/interrupt overload, not MTU. Any RDMA/roce enabled? We don't use RoCE on these SKUs.

sara: No RoCE. We do have jumbo frames enabled cluster-wide, but MTU logs show 9000 on both endpoints. I verified no single link mismatch.

kai: Repro steps on canary: synthetic batching load using our perf harness (burst size 64, concurrency 128). Increasing concurrency above 120 causes tx_ring_occupancy to jump and latency tails. Snapshot commands I ran: ```sudo ethtool -S eth0 | egrep 'tx_|rx_'``` and ```cat /proc/net/softnet_stat | sed -n '1p;2,8p'``` — softnet shows backlog spikes.

alex: We should check net.core.netdev_max_backlog and somaxconn. Current value is 1000 on affected nodes; softnet overflow counter increments in dmesg. Raising netdev_max_backlog to 5000 reduced immediate drops in canary.

mike: Also check tso/gso/gro. When bursts happen, large aggregated packets can create long processing on receiver side. Try toggling GRO off on canary as a quick test: `sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off` and run the harness.

sara: I ran that: disabling GRO reduced p99 from ~420ms to ~120ms but increased CPU sys%. So it's a tradeoff.

kai: We should tune irq affinity and XPS/RPS to spread load across cores. I saw IRQs pinned to core 3 and that core was saturated. Adding XPS masks for tx queues distributes processing.

alex: For longer-term, consider increasing tx ring size: `ethtool -G eth0 tx 4096` — current is 512. That reduced tx_dropped in a short test. Also set `net.core.rmem_max` and `wmem_max` higher.

mike: Could be NAPI starvation under extreme batching. Another mitigation: enable fairness in our batching scheduler to avoid sudden fan-out across nodes at identical boundaries — stagger batch flushes by +/- 50ms to smooth bursts.

sara: Agree. Short-term plan: 1) Apply netdev_max_backlog=5000 and ethtool -G tx 4096 on canary pool. 2) Disable GRO for one test group to confirm CPU vs latency tradeoff. 3) Add XPS mask changes to init scripts. 4) Stagger batch flushes in runtime canary. 5) Monitor for 24h.

mike: I'll open a quick runbook PR with the commands and rollback steps. @oncall-bot could you create an incident-ticket with severity-low and attach the perf graphs?

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-20260312-037. Attachments: grafana/us-west2/batching_p99.png, ethtool-snapshots.zip.

kai: One more thought — if we see repeated TX queue busy messages, we might need to upgrade NIC drivers or switch firmware; vendor had a known issue with queue starvation on heavy bursts (FW v2.1.3 vs v2.2.0). I'll check vendor notes and schedule a firmware window if required.

alex: Posted a short checklist in the runbook channel for triage steps (ip link, ethtool -S, /proc/net/softnet_stat, netstat -s, dmesg).

sara: After applying the backlog/ring changes on canary, p99 dropped ~3x during the next peak. We'll roll to 10% of production tomorrow 08:30 and monitor. I'll update this thread with telemetry. :thumbsup:

mike: Thanks — good catch. Also let's capture a packet trace (tcpdump -w) for one window next roll to rule out middlebox burst shaping.

sara: Will do. Timeline: changes deployed to canary at 18:45 UTC, initial rollout 10% tomorrow 08:30 UTC. Follow-ups in morning and after 24h.
